title: Versions
description: A short note on a warm white ground with its twelve earlier saves stacked behind it, receding in real perspective into a soft haze, each one's spine naming in a serif what that save changed, like the margin of a proof. Drag or scroll and you fly back through them: the front card swells and dissolves past you, the next save comes forward and settles on a soft spring with a small tick, and only the card at the front marks what that save changed, what it wrote inked in from the caret as a serif correction, the way a proofreader marks a page, and a fine red caret where words were taken out. When each was saved is set once, in a ruled margin beside the stack: a hairline a gutter clear of the front sheet, a short tick on it at every spine's baseline, and the date hanging off the rule on that line, so stack and margin are two columns joined by alignment, like the times down a tracklist.
intent: After macOS Time Machine's receding stack of window versions (https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/restore-files-mh11422/mac) and the Time Machine stack pattern on devouringdetails.com (https://devouringdetails.com): versions recede into depth and scrolling brings older states forward, here applied to the saves of one document with the diff shown only where you are looking.
